notes: Fresh independent source audit of pinned commit d912f0c06e7af29a4a40c4211bec0bb76d473f10. Read Inspector root AGENTS.md, contract and entire benchmark README; read OpenClaw root, extensions, plugin-sdk and plugins AGENTS.md. No Inspector implementation, helpers, detector output, other fixtures or extraction were used.

All 14 eligible production JS/TS-family files were manually read in full, including both declaration files, plus package and manifest metadata. Every plugin-root file is reviewed or explicitly excluded. Reviewed bytes match the pinned Git objects; root-authorized instructions changes do not affect plugin source.

Package build.staticAssets explicitly ships onepassword-op-path.js, onepassword-secret-ref-resolver.js and onepassword-secret-id.js. The independent resolver is production source even though it is not imported by index.ts. No production local import leaves the canonical plugin root; there is no additional plugin-owned/shared shipped source boundary. SDK implementations and installed dependencies are not recursively audited.

Test-support helpers were read and repository-wide caller searches proved exclusive test use; they are excluded individually. The SDK imports in memory-store.test-support.ts therefore do not become production dependencies.

definePluginEntry.register is typed as OpenClawPluginDefinition.register, which accepts OpenClawPluginApi. Its api.runtime member is PluginRuntime; direct maximal paths are normalized accordingly. No incidental api.runtime or runtime.state/config prefixes are emitted.

PluginStateKeyedStore values returned by openKeyedStore are SDK-returned store objects, not runtime handles; their entries/register/lookup/consume/delete methods do not invent runtime-member paths. Hook event/context fields, tool invocation context, command objects and fresh parsed configuration/broker objects similarly do not become API/runtime members. The unchanged raw api.pluginConfig passed into the local parser retains its original provenance, as reconciled separately below.

pluginSecretRefSetup is an imported SDK object: selecting resolveTrustedExecutablePath adds member-access and invoking the unchanged local alias adds call to that original exported-root identity. The separate resolveTrustedOnePasswordCli wrapper remains plugin-owned.

createPluginSecretRefSetupCli returns an adapter object. Calls to its inspectProvider/registerSetupCommand and the Parameters<typeof onePasswordSecretRefSetupCli.registerSetupCommand> query do not extend the original function export or create API/runtime findings. The factory import/call remains a runtime dependency.

Only agreed manifest contract fields are inventoried: cliCommands.name, commandAliases.name and contracts.tools. secretProviderIntegrations, activation, categories and configuration metadata are outside the frozen manifest identity set.

All explicit type imports and annotations remain type dependencies in this source phase. plugin-entry is mixed because its module has both ordinary definePluginEntry and explicit type import sites; OpenClawConfig retains separate identities at its two public source modules. Source scope is not an asserted published-artifact inventory.

findingCount counts distinct findings with evidence in each reviewed file. Evidence is representative per kind and relevant file; full source reading established the complete identity and reference-kind sets. No genuinely unresolved public dependency construct was found.

Original-owner source-only reconciliation: index.ts:24 passes api.pluginConfig unchanged through parseOnePasswordConfig(value), its unknown annotation and isRecord guard. Direct reads and literal-key local helper calls establish exactly seven additional runtime member-access identities: vault, defaultPolicy, items, opBin, cacheTtlSeconds, grantTtlHours and opTimeoutMs. requiredString/readOptionalOnePasswordString/readOnePasswordNumber preserve the input object at their record[key] reads; fallback values do not erase those possible original-object reads. Calls on strings and Object.keys remain JavaScript built-in behavior, not API calls.

The root api.pluginConfig.item, api.pluginConfig.description and api.pluginConfig.field identities are unwarranted: config.ts:94/103/109 pass rawItem from Object.entries(value.items) at line 87, a per-slug object rather than the top-level config. The per-item vault call at line 99 is likewise a separate context. No static slug establishes an exact nested identity. The fresh items map and item records at lines 86/115–121 and returned config object at lines 129–146 do not inherit the original root identity; downstream parsed-config reads and the arbitrary SDK result livePluginConfig add no such provenance.
